name: Delhivery Ltd
title: Delhivery Ltd - 543529 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Express volumes up ~72% with FY26 FCF turning positive at ₹89 cr and ROIC 16%; capex intensity down to 4.7% from 7.8%, but supply-side discipline is management's claim rather than a verified industry supply cut.

capex.peers_comment: Management said other players are unlikely to raise capital intensity because most do not run integrated networks; Ecom Express and XpressBees were said to have burned balance sheets.
capex.quote: I don't think that's very likely because most of them don't run integrated networks in the first place.

triggers.label: Capex intensity 7.8% → 4.7%
triggers.quote: CapEx as a percentage of revenue has been brought dow n diligently. We were at about 7.8% in FY23. That's come down all the way to 4.7% now.

triggers.label: Market structure more settled
triggers.quote: What you're seeing is more stable, long-term competitive dynamics as opposed to short-term price gouging

triggers.label: Fuel pass-through via diesel-linked contracts
triggers.quote: We have a natural pass -through process, where our prices are indexed to diesel prices at the pumps, especially in the PTL business.

triggers.label: Express volume 306 mn, ~72% growth
triggers.quote: Note that the volumes this quarter were 306 million, pretty encouraging.

triggers.label: Receivable days 38 → 11
triggers.quote: that's come down to 11 days, a very sharp drop in receivables.

guidance.quote: The express business remains firmly at the upper end of our normative margin guidance of 16 to 18%.
We will get to our 4% target.
Our anticipation of the investment fo r fiscal 27 is broadly between about 130 and 160 crores
the steady state ROICs, currently we are at 16%, but in a steady state, this number for our transport business can certainly go to 25% plus.

prior_guidance_check.quote: this is one year ahead of plan

red_flags.quote: while it's higher than the 16% that we were at last year

red_flags.quote: the working capital line items move fairly ferociously from 324 to 135

evasions.quote: it's too early for me to really comment here.
But Vani, Navneet, both of you are on this call.

summary.headline: Delhivery FY26 revenue reached ~10,486 crore with 7.3% service EBITDA and first full-year FCF positive at ~89 crore, a year ahead of plan.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was about 2,848 crore with PAT of about 87 crore (~3% margin) and adjusted EBITDA of 151 crore. FY26 was the first year of the Ecom Express integration, with over a billion express packages and about 2 million MT of PTL freight. Supply chain services (SCS) reached breakeven on adjusted EBITDA after a service EBITDA turnaround to 10.9%. Management said the company turned FCF positive, one year ahead of plan, despite integration costs; cash stood above 4,500 crore.

segments.name: Express
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue ~1,832 crore, up 46% YoY, with volumes of 306 million (up ~72-73% YoY, sequentially up on Q3). FY26 revenue ~6,685 crore and about a billion parcels; service EBITDA at upper end of 16-18% normative range.

segments.name: Part Truck Load (PTL)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue ~622 crore and 549 thousand MT, both up ~20% YoY. FY26 about 2 million MT and ~2,254 crore revenue; management cited gross margin rising from 14% to 28% over roughly 2.5-3 years.

segments.name: Supply Chain Services (SCS)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue ~729 crore with service EBITDA of 10.9% (~79 crore), up ~4x; segment at breakeven on adjusted EBITDA. Two mandates signed and activated in Q4.

segments.name: Delhivery Direct (intracity and intercity)
segments.commentary: Intracity on-demand service live in six cities; FY26 investment about 76 crore, with FY27 investment guided at 130-160 crore toward a 200+ crore external GMV run-rate.

guidance_outlook: Long-term transport ROIC target of 25%+, with adjusted EBITDA rising from ~6.3% toward at least 10%, and PTL service EBITDA moving toward ~18% and corporate overheads falling to ~7% of revenue.
Capital intensity (capex plus working-capital items) of ~21.5% of revenue could fall by 2-3 percentage points.
Capex to reach the 4% of revenue target from 4.7%; AGV and automation spend not expected to materially change capex guidance.
Net working capital at 11 days seen as sustainable; further reduction possible via faster billing and prepaid mix, though with limits.
FY27 new-business investment of 130-160 crore guided in the shareholder letter.
Management expects e-commerce industry to grow 15-20% in the medium term.
Management said the company does not plan a broad price increase now, though diesel pass-through clauses apply to PTL and some customers.
capex_capacity: Capex fell to 4.7% of revenue (from 7.8% in FY23); management reiterated a 4% target and said it is moving slightly ahead of plan.
Fleet metric: the 20,000 daily average fleet figure covers only contracted monthly vehicles; the decline reflects a shift to per-kilo variable fleet, while tractor-trailer count rose QoQ.
AGV pilots in Mumbai (Bombay) to be expanded to other mega gateways within FY27.
Delhivery Labs launched about a year ago; AI and automation deployed in claims, documentation and customer communication.
Company is the first in India to get a road train, after a 46-foot tractor trailer launch.
demand_pricing: Management said market structure is more settled after the Ecom Express deal, with less short-term price gouging than in the two years before FY26.
Share of 1P (first-party) logistics declined over the last year, per a listed marketplace; management expects a gradual shift towards 3P.
Long-tail D2C/SME share described as stable to slightly up YoY; heavy shipping share described as dominant.
Single largest customer was ~16% of revenue last year; management said it is well below its informal 35% concern threshold.

Diesel price hikes of about Rs 3/litre at pumps: prices indexed for PTL; express pass-through is via DPH clauses assessed customer by customer. Rs 1-2 price increases seen in some air-network pockets via surcharges.
Management dismissed Amazon's reopening of its 3PL offering as an old product with limited strategic value.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of rising fuel prices on consumption and costs, and has Delhivery raised prices?
qa_highlights.answer: PTL prices are diesel-indexed; express uses DPH clauses. Pump prices rose about Rs 3, and no broad price hike is planned. Q4 margins rose over Q3 despite fuel, and a volatile environment is seen as favourable to the market leader.

qa_highlights.question: Is Amazon's 3PL push a competitive threat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it an old product in a new wrapper; first-party orders get priority at last mile and first-party logistics costs more than 3PL when fully loaded.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the working capital reduction, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Drivers included faster and more accurate billing, client selection (declining some RFQs), and more-than-monthly billing for preferential pricing. NWC was 11 days versus 38 three years ago; management called it sustainable.

qa_highlights.question: Will SCS pipeline remain margin accretive, and how much of new initiatives' investment is opex?
qa_highlights.answer: Each SCS project must clear an internal hurdle rate and the pipeline is in focus sectors. Short-term start-up costs can weigh on P&L. Management did not give a split of the 130-160 crore FY27 spend between opex and capex in the call.

qa_highlights.question: Will capex intensity rise with express growth, and will the industry overbuild?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex intensity is expected to stay around the 4% target; growth is mainly PTL and heavy, and management does not expect irrational pricing like three or four years ago.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Delhivery Direct opportunity and investment?
qa_highlights.answer: Intracity service live in six cities; FY26 spend ~76 crore; FY27 guided at 130-160 crore toward 200+ crore external GMV run-rate. Management described the TAM as very large without quantifying it.

qa_highlights.question: Is PTL leadership achievable, and what capabilities are missing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited PTL growth from ~280-290k tons to ~550k tons per quarter over 2-3 years with gross margin from 14% to 28%. Varun Bakshi said the playbook is share-of-wallet expansion with key accounts.

risks_watch: Fuel-price pass-through: the impact on volumes and consumption is not yet quantified; management said Q2 would show more.
Competitive dynamics from 1P marketplaces insourcing or reopening 3PL offerings, plus possible share shifts in key accounts.
Labour cost inflation from minimum wage and gig worker laws, and potential increase in service costs.
Concentration: the largest customer rose above 16% of revenue; management says it is not near its informal 35% limit.
Working capital at 11 days may be hard to sustain; management flagged limits on further billing-cycle gains.
New businesses (Delhivery Direct, Rapid, SCS pipeline) carry 130-160 crore of FY27 investment that could weigh on margins.
Management noted a 'volatile start' to FY27 without details.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on profitability, FCF and market position, with specific numeric targets. Cautious and somewhat deflective on fuel-price consumption impact, saying it is too early to quantify, and on the ex-Ecom FCF question.
key_quotes: So, in effect, we are signing off FY26 with strong fundamentals across every line of business.
The core is profitable. The core is cash generative. SCS is pivoted.
But I'll be honest, Mukesh, I've been saying this for three years now. I don't lose a lot of sleep over this and I don't think our customers do either.
The steady state ROICs, currently we are at 16%, but in a steady state, this number for our transport business can certainly go to 25% plus.

financial_highlights.value: 7.3% (~764 crore) as stated; adjusted EBITDA ~457 crore / 4.4% cited for the segment P&L
financial_highlights.change: Service EBITDA up ~220 bps to 15.6% for transport (express + PTL)
One year ahead of plan; management said it absorbed integration costs

AGV automation pilots in Mumbai, to be expanded to other mega gateways within FY27

growth.why: No explicit FY27 revenue growth number is guided; management points to Express margin at upper end of 16-18%, transport adjusted EBITDA rising from ~6.3% toward 10%+ via PTL margin and overhead cuts, and FY27 new-business investment of 130-160 crore, backed by partial specifics (six-city Direct rollout, Mumbai AGV pilots) rather than firm capacity or order numbers.
